exposure: rupture of grade 3 or 4 during delivery
cohort: 400 women interviewed in the first 48 h after childbirth in Torbate-heydariyeh (eastern Iran) in 2015.
finding: The prevalence of traumatic childbirth was 48.3%, and risk factors included place of residence, type of delivery, pregnancy complications, bleeding during pregnancy, rupture of grade 3 or 4 during delivery, and emergency cesarean section.
mod_finding: Type of delivery and emergency cesarean section were significantly correlated with traumatic childbirth.
